entry.title: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems
entry.summary: Four days of brilliant argument about whether the Earth moves — the vernacular bestseller that got its author hauled before the Inquisition, translated from Galileo's own Italian.

entry.title: Conversations on the Plurality of Worlds
entry.summary: Six evenings in a moonlit park: a young philosopher teaches a witty Marquise the new astronomy and the plurality of worlds. Retold from the French of 1686.
entry.content: Six evenings in a moonlit park: a young philosopher teaches a witty Marquise the new astronomy and the plurality of worlds. Retold from the French of 1686.

entry.title: Letters to a German Princess
entry.summary: The great mathematician's 234 letters teaching a fifteen-year-old princess science and philosophy, 1760 to 1762, translated from the French.
entry.content: The great mathematician's 234 letters teaching a fifteen-year-old princess science and philosophy, 1760 to 1762, translated from the French.

entry.title: On the Origin of Species
entry.summary: One long argument that changed biology forever: variation, inheritance, and the struggle for existence add up to natural selection — and to the common descent of all living things.
entry.content: One long argument that changed biology forever: variation, inheritance, and the struggle for existence add up to natural selection — and to the common descent of all living things.

entry.title: On the Various Forces of Nature
entry.summary: Six Christmas lectures for young people on gravitation, cohesion, chemical affinity, heat, magnetism and electricity — arriving at the conclusion that they are not six powers at all but one, convertible each into the others.
entry.content: Six Christmas lectures for young people on gravitation, cohesion, chemical affinity, heat, magnetism and electricity — arriving at the conclusion that they are not six powers at all but one, convertible each into the others.

entry.title: The Chemical History of a Candle
entry.summary: Six Christmas lectures for young people at the Royal Institution, drawing the whole of chemistry out of a single burning candle — where it gets its fuel, why the flame is bright, what it consumes, what it makes, and why you yourself are a slow candle.
entry.content: Six Christmas lectures for young people at the Royal Institution, drawing the whole of chemistry out of a single burning candle — where it gets its fuel, why the flame is bright, what it consumes, what it makes, and why you yourself are a slow candle.

entry.title: Sound
entry.summary: The lectures on sound that founded a tradition — from the row of boys who pass a push down a line to the fog-signal researches that overturned everything the age believed about sound at sea.
entry.content: The lectures on sound that founded a tradition — from the row of boys who pass a push down a line to the fog-signal researches that overturned everything the age believed about sound at sea.

entry.title: Star-land
entry.summary: Six Royal Institution Christmas lectures taking young people from the sun out to the nebulae — with a closing chapter that teaches you to find your own way around the constellations tonight.

entry.title: Soap Bubbles and the Forces Which Mould Them
entry.summary: Why a bubble is round, why a falling jet of water breaks into beads, and how a fountain can be made to sing a tune — three Christmas lectures on surface tension, given to a hall full of children and illustrated with all sixty-nine of the original plates.

entry.title: Light Visible and Invisible
entry.summary: Six Royal Institution Christmas lectures on light — from ripples in a tank of water to the X-rays discovered thirteen months before the first lecture was given.

entry.title: Waves and Ripples in Water, Air, and Aether
entry.summary: Six Christmas lectures for young people at the Royal Institution on waves of every kind — ripples on a pond, the wake of a ship, sound and music, electric oscillations, and the waves by which Marconi had just begun to signal across the sea.
